objective: Compute a posterior over the lab's benchmark score against the other entrants by bootstrapping over cases, so the house can state a probability of rank rather than a point standing, kept strictly internal and never attached to any submission
rationale: The lab's standing is a mean over eight cases and the margin is thin against per-case dispersion that is not thin, which is the exact situation where a point ranking misleads. The round-5 overall stands at 0.0566 against the next entrant at 0.0595, a margin of 0.002878 on an eight-case mean, while our own per-case scores span 0.0353 to 0.1011, and we lead on four of the eight cases, down from five the round before. Per-case scores exist for all five entrants, so a case-level bootstrap of the rank is directly computable from the standings table with no new data and no new evaluation. The record also contains the case that makes this more than an exercise: one duct case regressed by 0.0029 in the same round, the regression was priced in writing and accepted before the scoring call, and it lost a tie that had been held by a margin of 0.00003. A point standing cannot express how fragile a margin of that size is, and a posterior can. The discipline around it matters as much as the number. Submission actions are parked by standing instruction and the lab has never submitted anything; the scoring is local, at a pinned benchmark commit, and the record says so in several places. So this item is filed explicitly as internal only: it produces a number for the house to reason with, it is not a submission action, it does not prepare one, and it does not treat a send as pending work. The honest caveats belong in the output rather than around it: bootstrapping eight cases gives a coarse posterior, the cases are not exchangeable since the duct cases and the wall-mounted case behave differently under the same term, and the other entrants' scores are fixed published numbers rather than samples, so what is being resampled is case selection and not their methods. Axis A: report-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0, and it changes no scored column.

cost_basis: measured; the per-case standings for all five entrants are already recorded at a pinned benchmark commit and the bootstrap is arithmetic over that table, so no solver time is spent, no case is opened and no evaluation is re-run
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes and each changes how the house talks about its own standing. One: the probability of leading is high and stable under resampling, which means the margin is real despite being thin and the lab can say so internally with a number instead of a mean. Two: it is near a coin flip, which is the most likely outcome given a margin of 0.002878 against per-case dispersion an order larger, and it would correct an internal habit of treating the standing as settled. Three: the posterior is dominated by one or two cases, which identifies exactly where the standing is fragile and is the same diagnostic the earlier error decomposition produced by a different route, giving an independent check on it. In every branch the lab learns what an eight-case mean can and cannot support.
in_sample_verdict: Not applicable and it cannot become applicable. Nothing is fitted, inverted or calibrated; no test data is read beyond scores already computed and recorded; no model is trained and no scored column moves. The item produces a probability about a table of numbers that already exists.
sequencing: Dispatchable now, zero solver cost. INTERNAL ONLY: submissions are parked by standing instruction, this item is not a submission action, it does not prepare one, and its output is not to be attached to any external package or treated as evidence that a send is pending.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Probability of rank: before any future leaderboard submission, a posterior over our score vs the board (bootstrap over cases) -- "P(rank 1) = x%" -- internal only, but it is the house asking the right question.' Operationalised: a case-level bootstrap over the eight scored cases using the recorded per-case scores for all five entrants at the pinned benchmark commit, reporting the probability of each rank for the lab's entry with the resampling unit stated, plus a leave-one-case-out sensitivity naming which cases the posterior depends on. The output carries three caveats on its face: the scoring is local and nothing has been submitted; the cases are not exchangeable and the bootstrap assumes they are; the other entrants' scores are fixed published values, so case selection is what is resampled. The number is internal and marked so; publishing it externally, or citing it in any submission-facing document, is outside this item.
supersession_note: SUPERSEDED IN PART on 2026-08-10 by chief ruling, recorded here 2026-08-11. The internal-only restriction this item carries in four decided fields -- objective ("kept strictly internal and never attached to any submission"), rationale ("this item is filed explicitly as internal only"), sequencing ("INTERNAL ONLY: ... its output is not to be attached to any external package") and gate ("The number is internal and marked so; publishing it externally, or citing it in any submission-facing document, is outside this item") -- was WITHDRAWN by the chief AFTER this item was approved and executed. Those four fields are left exactly as decided and are deliberately not rewritten: re-authoring a decided field under an unchanged decided_at would forge the record of what was approved on what grounds, which is the failure this lab's supersede-don't-delete convention exists to prevent. The withdrawal's reason, so it is not lost with the rule: Ladder V's cold-reproduction pass recomputed the figure as 0.674 from public data -- the benchmark README's published board plus the lab's own eight submission CSVs -- in about a minute, with no access to the internal document. A figure an outsider reproduces trivially is not protected by being withheld; withholding buys nothing and only looks concealed, and it looks that way to exactly the reader the lab's disclosure strategy exists to convince. The figure now TRAVELS with the entry. One prohibition replaces the gate: no surface may state the figure without its interval. Every rank claim, internal or external, carries P(rank 1) = 68% (67.6% over 400,000 case-level bootstrap resamples) together with its interval -- 2-100% at 95% by double bootstrap, since eight cases cannot pin it tighter -- and the not-decided pairs: the leads over Reissmann and Wu & Zhang are not statistically decided, while the leads over Liu and Montoya are, at 98.7% and 99.8%. Everything else this item decided stands unchanged: zero solver core-min, zero scoring calls, the lab's scoring-call ledger still at 6, the resampling unit stated, the leave-one-case-out sensitivity delivered, and the three caveats the gate required on the output's face. Status stays approved; only the publication restriction fell.
